reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Shared global rules of the road
themes.definition: Calls for common international rules, safeguards, norms and possibly new institutions or a framework convention to govern AI.
themes.inclusion: Include passages calling for common rules, safeguards, global guardrails, a framework convention, or IAEA/ITU-like institutions for AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages that only describe UN bodies without calling for rules.
themes.boundary_cases: Proposals for a UN framework convention count here and in AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: We must urgently establish common rules and safeguards for AI.
we must collectively formulate new rules and be prepared to create new institutions if necessary for new technologies

themes.label: UN AI bodies as convergence venue
themes.definition: Support for UN-specific AI processes (High-Level Advisory Body, Scientific Panel, Global Dialogue, Global Digital Compact, OEWG) and the UN as the universal venue for AI norms.
themes.inclusion: Include welcomes of UN AI bodies/reports and claims that the UN has a critical role in AI governance.
themes.exclusion: Exclude calls for rules that name no UN body or role.
themes.boundary_cases: Lessons from the ICT OEWG applied to AI count here.

examples.quote: Singapore welcomes the report of the High-Level Advisory Body on AI
The UN, the United Nations, has a critical role to play in building convergence

themes.label: Loss of control and frontier AI safeguards
themes.definition: Technical AI safety concerns: loss of control of autonomous systems, WMD misuse by rogue actors, testing and evaluation, incident reporting, human control.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on loss of control, testing/evaluation before deployment, frontier model safety, or keeping humans in control.
themes.exclusion: Exclude battlefield or nuclear command uses of AI (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS) unless framed as general safety.
themes.boundary_cases: The 'nuclear button' thought experiment is used to illustrate human control generally; code here and AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.

examples.quote: First, the loss of control of autonomous systems.
We need rigorous testing and evaluation before deployment.

themes.label: AI in conflict and nuclear escalation
themes.definition: Risks of AI in conflict situations and nuclear decision-making, raising miscalculation and escalation risk.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on AI in conflict, military systems, or control of nuclear weapons.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general loss-of-control safety concerns not tied to conflict.
themes.boundary_cases: Rogue actors using AI for bioweapons is closer to AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL/misuse than state military use.

examples.quote: the advent of artificial intelligence in conflict situations has actually increased the risks exponentially
Do you want the nuclear button to be in the hands of a human being or an AI?

themes.label: Powerful engine needs good brakes
themes.definition: Framing AI as both extraordinary potential and peril, requiring innovation and safeguards together.
themes.inclusion: Include explicit promise/peril pairings or engine-and-brakes metaphors.
themes.exclusion: Exclude one-sided benefit or risk statements.
themes.boundary_cases: Where the duality leads to a governance call, code both.

examples.quote: By now, the promises and the perils of AI are well known to all of us.
every powerful engine needs good brakes, safeguards

themes.label: Skills-driven AI productivity gains
themes.definition: AI as a productivity engine requiring investment in skills, talent and infrastructure so workers and businesses can redesign work.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on productivity gains from AI and equipping workers with AI skills.
themes.exclusion: Exclude capacity support to other countries (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
themes.boundary_cases: Domestic skills investment for small states may also be AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: The real productivity gains from AI comes not from the IT department, but from our businesses and workers having the skills

value.rationale: Singapore's speeches consistently pair AI's potential with safety risks and call for global rules centred on UN processes; 2026 adds detailed technical safety (testing, loss of control), strategic competition and productivity/skills, while 2023 emphasises AI in conflict.
